clusters.rule: Do not change the unique_id format of entities that already shipped; leave existing suffixes untouched and only apply a new scheme to newly added entities.
clusters.trigger: A diff edits the f-string that builds `_attr_unique_id` for an entity class that already exists in a released integration.
clusters.rationale: Changing a shipped unique_id orphans the entity registry entries users already have, so they lose history and customisations; a new scheme is only safe for entities that have never been released.

clusters.rule: Polling and update-interval constants must match the cadence stated in the integration's README, inline comments and the PR description; change the constant or the documentation so they agree.
clusters.trigger: A diff adds or changes a `*_UPDATE_DELAY` / `MIN_TIME_BETWEEN_UPDATES` / `SCAN_INTERVAL` constant to a value different from the interval documented for that integration.
clusters.rationale: Reviewers check the poll cadence against what the integration documents and what the PR claims; a silent mismatch misleads users about the load placed on the vendor API.

clusters.rule: An entity factory must not return None for arbitrary unknown description keys; restrict the skip to the intended conditional entities and log or raise for keys that are missing from the mapping.
clusters.trigger: A create_sensor/create_entity helper gains a broad `if key not in self.services: return None` guard in front of the mapping lookup.
clusters.rationale: A blanket 'unknown key returns None' guard silently drops entities when a description key is mistyped or removed; only the intended conditional entities should be skippable.

clusters.rule: A missing or None device value must surface as unknown and be handled explicitly; never let it collapse into the false/off branch, whether it drives an entity's state, its identity or its translation key.
clusters.trigger: A state property or conditional written as `result.get(key) == "0"`, `bool(data.get(key, False))`, or `"a" if flag else "b"` where the underlying lookup can return None.
clusters.rationale: Home Assistant distinguishes unknown from off, so folding an absent reading into False makes the UI and automations assert something the device never reported.

clusters.rule: Sanitize any user-provided value used as a statistic_id prefix (slugify or replace separators such as '-'), do not merely lowercase it, before calling async_add_external_statistics.
clusters.trigger: A coordinator builds a statistic_id from config entry data with `.lower()` or direct interpolation and passes it to async_add_external_statistics / async_import_statistics.
clusters.rationale: Recorder statistic ids are parsed on ':' and must be valid object ids, so a user-supplied account name containing separators corrupts the external statistics table.

clusters.rule: Integration service handlers must raise ServiceValidationError when the config entry they need is missing or not loaded, instead of failing with a generic or unhandled error.
clusters.trigger: A service handler resolves a config entry (or requires a loaded entry) and raises HomeAssistantError, asserts, or proceeds without a ServiceValidationError path.
clusters.rationale: ServiceValidationError is the class the frontend renders as a user mistake rather than an integration crash, so a missing or unloaded entry must raise it.

clusters.rule: Every reason passed to async_abort in a config flow or subentry flow must have a key in that flow's `abort` block in strings.json; keys defined only under `error` are not used for aborts.
clusters.trigger: A flow calls `self.async_abort(reason="cannot_connect")` (or similar) while strings.json defines that key only under `config_subentries.<type>.error` / `config.error`.
clusters.rationale: Config flow aborts look up strings.json under `abort`; a key defined only under `error` renders as an untranslated reason to the user.

clusters.rule: Register the teardown of any connection or resource opened in async_setup_entry with entry.async_on_unload (or close it in the failure path) before calling async_config_entry_first_refresh.
clusters.trigger: async_setup_entry opens a client/connection, then calls async_config_entry_first_refresh, with the close registered only in async_unload_entry.
clusters.rationale: If the first refresh fails, setup raises before async_unload_entry ever runs, so a connection whose close is registered only there leaks on every retry.

clusters.rule: Test fixtures and mocked client returns must reproduce what the real library or device produces: typed objects where the library returns typed objects, the upstream key casing and payload shape rather than the integration's post-processed form, and device metadata consistent with the datapoints the fixture declares.
clusters.trigger: A conftest or fixture file supplying plain dicts/MagicMocks where the library returns typed objects, already-normalised keys (snake_case where the API sends camelCase), or a device fixture whose product name and category do not match its datapoint set.
clusters.rationale: Mocks more forgiving than the real library hide attribute-versus-item and shape errors until users hit them; these fixtures are the only description of the upstream contract this repo has.

clusters.rule: Diagnostics code must use Home Assistant's shared redaction helpers and REDACTED constant rather than hard-coding a redaction marker string.
clusters.trigger: A diagnostics.py module writes a literal like `"**REDACTED**"` in a custom scrubbing function instead of importing the constant used by async_redact_data.
clusters.rationale: Redaction is centralised in Home Assistant's diagnostics helpers so the marker stays identical across every integration's downloadable diagnostics.

clusters.rule: Device- or feature-specific trigger logic added to a shared entity class must be gated on the entity description key / event type it belongs to, not applied to every instance of the class.
clusters.trigger: A shared entity's _async_update_attrs stops consulting `self._event` (or the description key) and keys off a device-specific field such as `doorbell_seq` for all instances.
clusters.rationale: A shared entity class is instantiated for every description key, so an ungated device-specific branch changes behaviour for devices the PR never considered.

clusters.rule: A configuration entity whose value can be changed outside Home Assistant and receives no push updates must be disabled by default and set _attr_should_poll with a long SCAN_INTERVAL, mirroring the existing pattern in the integration.
clusters.trigger: A new EntityCategory.CONFIG number/select entity is added with neither _attr_should_poll/SCAN_INTERVAL nor entity_registry_enabled_default=False, while sibling config entities in the same integration set both.
clusters.rationale: A value changeable outside Home Assistant goes stale without polling, and the integration's existing config entities already establish the disabled-by-default plus long SCAN_INTERVAL pattern.

clusters.rule: Entity names in strings.json must use sentence case, matching the surrounding entries.
clusters.trigger: A strings.json diff adds an entity `name` with title-cased words (e.g. "Sync Date and Time") while neighbouring names are sentence case.
clusters.rationale: Sentence case is the Home Assistant UI standard for entity names, and mixed casing inside one strings.json is immediately visible to users.

clusters.rule: Entity-platform tests must pin the exact set of entities a setup produces - snapshot them, or assert the precise expected entities per affected device type - never a smoke check that setup did not crash or a `>=` lower bound.
clusters.trigger: A test asserting `len(states) >= N`, or only that setup succeeded, for a platform or device-type-to-description mapping the diff changes.
clusters.rationale: Loose assertions keep passing while entities silently appear or disappear, which is exactly the regression a change to these mappings causes for users.

clusters.rule: Define a value used by more than one module once and import it - in the integration's const.py for code, in the shared test module for tests - rather than repeating the literal or the definition in a second module.
clusters.trigger: A constant, command map or tuning literal (delay, timeout, threshold, TEST_*) added to a platform, __init__.py, services.py, conftest.py or a test module while the same value is already named in that integration's const.py or another of its modules.
clusters.rationale: Duplicated definitions drift apart silently; the repo keeps one authoritative definition per integration so a change lands everywhere at once.

clusters.rule: Entity-registry migrations that match legacy unique_ids must derive the legacy prefix from the exact value that originally built those ids, and the tests must cover the case where that value differs from the config entry host.
clusters.trigger: A migration filters entity registry entries with `entity_entry.unique_id.startswith(config_entry.data[CONF_HOST])` when the old unique_id was built from a different source (API hostname, serial, etc.).
clusters.rationale: Legacy unique_ids were built from whatever value the old code used, so matching on the current config entry host silently skips every install where the two differ.

clusters.rule: value_fn lambdas in entity descriptions must match the signature of the helper they call; do not rely on the platform's TypeError handling in native_value to absorb a mismatch.
clusters.trigger: An entity description passes `value=lambda data, k=...: helper(data, k)` while the helper is declared to take a different argument (e.g. a single typed object).
clusters.rationale: The comment fixes one lambda whose arguments did not match the helper it calls; the general form is 'call functions with the right arguments', not a Home Assistant convention.

clusters.rule: Do not override async_toggle on light entities; rely on the default ToggleEntity implementation that calls async_turn_on/async_turn_off.
clusters.trigger: A light platform defines `async def async_toggle` that forwards to a device/library toggle call.
clusters.rationale: ToggleEntity already implements async_toggle in terms of async_turn_on/async_turn_off, so an override duplicates core logic and skips the state handling core performs.

clusters.rule: Code that reads coordinator data must match the payload shape actually stored in coordinator.data (as shown by the diagnostics snapshots); convert payloads into typed objects consistently before storing them rather than assuming attributes on raw dicts.
clusters.trigger: A helper iterates `self.data["..."].values()` and accesses attributes (`zone_data.ac_power`) on entries the coordinator stores as raw API dicts.
clusters.rationale: Whatever _async_update_data stores is what every entity and the diagnostics dump reads, so mixing raw API dicts with typed models makes attribute access fail for only some devices.

clusters.rule: Never call a synchronous vendor-library method directly from async code; wrap it in hass.async_add_executor_job (or expose it as a non-async accessor), especially when the same call is already treated as blocking elsewhere in the integration.
clusters.trigger: An `async def` method returns or awaits the result of a sync library call such as `self._tado.rate_limit_info()` with no executor job.
clusters.rationale: A blocking library call in the event loop stalls all of Home Assistant, so the repo requires hass.async_add_executor_job for any synchronous I/O.

clusters.rule: Pass only raw identifiers (entity_id, chat_id) in translation_placeholders and keep the explanatory wording inside the translation string itself.
clusters.trigger: A ServiceValidationError/HomeAssistantError raised with translation_placeholders whose value is an f-string containing English prose such as f"Notify entity not found: {entity_id}".
clusters.rationale: Translators can only translate the string itself, so English prose smuggled in through a placeholder is never translated.

clusters.rule: When a shared config-flow helper such as validate_input gains a new branch, add test coverage for every flow that calls it, including reauth.
clusters.trigger: A diff adds a fallback or conditional inside validate_input() (or another helper shared by user/DHCP/reauth steps) while the test diff only touches the user or discovery flow.
clusters.rationale: validate_input is shared by the user, discovery and reauth steps, so a new branch there changes flows the PR's tests never touch.

clusters.rule: Annotate values that hold Home Assistant unit constants with their enum type (e.g. UnitOfTemperature) rather than str.
clusters.trigger: An attribute or return annotation typed str while the value comes from hass.config.units.temperature_unit or a UnitOfTemperature member.
clusters.rationale: Home Assistant's unit constants are StrEnums; typing them as str loses the checking that catches a raw string passed where a unit is required.

clusters.rule: Numeric state validation for template entities must keep booleans invalid; test with type(result) in (int, float) instead of isinstance.
clusters.trigger: A numeric-state check in a template platform written as isinstance(result, (int, float)).
clusters.rationale: bool is a subclass of int, so isinstance lets True through as a numeric state and the template sensor publishes a boolean as a number.

clusters.rule: Template entity setup helpers must raise or log when their backing option is unset instead of silently doing nothing.
clusters.trigger: setup_state_template() or a sibling setup_* helper on TemplateEntity/TriggerEntity that returns early when the corresponding _*_option attribute is None.
clusters.rationale: Silently returning when the backing option is unset leaves the entity permanently blank with nothing in the log to explain why.

clusters.rule: Do not raise repair issues off a template render that failed; only compare against a successfully rendered result.
clusters.trigger: A repair issue (async_create_issue / async_create_*_issue) created after assigning `result or []` from a template render that can yield None.
clusters.rationale: A failed render yields None, so raising a repair issue from it reports a configuration problem the user does not actually have.

clusters.rule: In config flow tests take the flow id from the result returned by start_reauth_flow rather than re-fetching it via hass.config_entries.flow.async_progress().
clusters.trigger: A test calls entry.start_reauth_flow(hass) and then asserts on async_progress() to obtain flows[0]["flow_id"].
clusters.rationale: start_reauth_flow already returns the flow result; re-fetching through async_progress couples the test to global flow state and breaks when another flow is in progress.

clusters.rule: Pass hass as the first argument to ConfigEntry.async_create_background_task, or use hass.async_create_background_task when entry lifecycle tying is not needed.
clusters.trigger: entry.async_create_background_task( called with only a coroutine and a name.
clusters.rationale: ConfigEntry.async_create_background_task takes hass so the task is tied to the entry's lifecycle and cancelled on unload.

clusters.rule: Trigger entry reloads from coordinator/runtime callbacks with hass.config_entries.async_schedule_reload, and update the tracked baseline so the condition cannot re-fire.
clusters.trigger: A coordinator update handler that compares against cached known_* state and schedules hass.config_entries.async_reload on every difference.
clusters.rationale: Calling async_reload from inside a coordinator callback reloads the entry that is currently running that callback; async_schedule_reload defers it, and the tracked baseline must move or the condition re-fires forever.

clusters.rule: Only pass translation_placeholders that the referenced translation string actually consumes, and do not source them from library exception attributes that may not exist.
clusters.trigger: UpdateFailed/HomeAssistantError raised with translation_placeholders whose keys do not appear in the integration's strings.json entry, or built from e.message.
clusters.rationale: Unused or missing placeholders fail at render time, and library exception attributes such as .message are not guaranteed to exist.

clusters.rule: A coordinator that translates one client exception must translate all of the client errors its calls can raise, including aiohttp.ClientConnectionError.
clusters.trigger: _async_update_data adds an `except ClientResponseError` branch raising a translated UpdateFailed while other aiohttp errors reachable from the same call stay unhandled.
clusters.rationale: A partially translated exception path means users get a clean message for one failure mode and a raw traceback for the next one from the same call.

clusters.rule: Match todo items by casefolding both the requested value and the stored uid/summary rather than comparing against a tuple of raw values.
clusters.trigger: An intent or service handler comparing a user-supplied item against todo_item.uid / todo_item.summary with `in (...)`.
clusters.rationale: Users say the item name in whatever case they like, so matching against a tuple of raw stored values makes the intent fail on capitalisation alone.

clusters.rule: Set _attr_unique_id once in __init__ from identifiers known at setup; never assign or recompute it inside update() or a coordinator callback.
clusters.trigger: An assignment to self._attr_unique_id (or self.entity_id-derived ids) inside update(), async_update(), or _handle_coordinator_update().
clusters.rationale: The entity registry reads unique_id when the entity is added, so recomputing it during an update either does nothing or creates a second registry entry.

clusters.rule: Entity descriptions must be defined inside the integration; map external quirk/library keys onto Home Assistant owned EntityDescription objects instead of synthesizing descriptions from library data.
clusters.trigger: A helper that constructs an EntityDescription with key=<library quirk attribute> from an object supplied by the vendor library or quirks registry.
clusters.rationale: Entity descriptions carry translation keys, device classes and enabled-by-default decisions that Home Assistant owns; synthesising them from library data moves those decisions outside this repo's review.

clusters.rule: When a Tuya device category is aliased to another category on one platform, add the same alias on every platform that already supports that category.
clusters.trigger: A new DeviceCategory entry added to a platform description map without the matching CATEGORY[DeviceCategory.X] = CATEGORY[DeviceCategory.Y] alias present in the sibling platforms.
clusters.rationale: Tuya category aliases are per-platform maps, so adding one on a single platform gives the device entities on that platform only and silently omits the rest.

clusters.rule: Factor repeated per-platform quirk registry lookup and entity construction into a shared helper module rather than copying the pattern into each platform.
clusters.trigger: A third or later platform file adding its own _get_quirk_entities() with the same TUYA_QUIRKS_REGISTRY.get_quirk_for_device + list comprehension shape.
clusters.rationale: The quirk registry lookup is identical on every platform, so a third copy means every future fix has to be made in every platform file.

clusters.rule: When one device yields several entities on the same platform, include a per-entity suffix in the unique_id so the entities cannot collide in the registry.
clusters.trigger: A list comprehension creating multiple entities of the same class from one device object where unique_id derives only from the device id.
clusters.rationale: Two entities of the same class from one device collide in the entity registry and one of them is dropped.

clusters.rule: Unit conversion must run device-native to entity unit when reading a property and entity to device unit when writing, so set/read round-trips agree.
clusters.trigger: A TemperatureConverter.convert (or similar) call in a state property whose from/to arguments are the reverse of the matching call in async_set_*.
clusters.rationale: If read and write convert in the same direction, setting a temperature and reading it back disagree and the value drifts on every round trip.

clusters.rule: Resolve an entity's native unit through the fixed precedence: no device_class first, then a device-reported unit, then NUMBER_DEVICE_CLASS_UNITS, then DEVICE_CLASS_UNITS, then the description default, and only finally drop the device_class.
clusters.trigger: A new branch inserted into _validate_device_class_unit or an equivalent unit-resolution routine ahead of the existing DEVICE_CLASS_UNITS checks.
clusters.rationale: The unit resolution order decides whether a device_class survives, so a branch inserted ahead of the existing checks changes units for devices the PR never looked at.

clusters.rule: Energy sensor entity descriptions must set suggested_display_precision alongside native and suggested units so the registry options match the snapshots.
clusters.trigger: A SensorEntityDescription with device_class=SensorDeviceClass.ENERGY that sets native_unit_of_measurement but no suggested_display_precision.
clusters.rationale: Energy entities without a display precision get registry options that differ from the snapshots and show users unrounded values.

clusters.rule: Name and translate a config switch after the setting it toggles, not after the action the underlying device performs.
clusters.trigger: A SwitchEntityDescription with entity_category=CONFIG whose translation_key reads as an imperative action (trigger_*, start_*) for a device capability that is merely enabled.
clusters.rationale: A config switch names the setting that is on or off; an imperative name reads like a button and misleads users about what toggling it does.

clusters.rule: A test covering a translated error must assert the exception's translation_domain and translation_key rather than merely that a HomeAssistantError was raised, and a platform that gains such a raise must gain the matching failure test.
clusters.trigger: pytest.raises(HomeAssistantError) around a service or entity action without asserting the translation key, or a new try/except raising a translated HomeAssistantError in a platform with no failure test at all.
clusters.rationale: Only the domain and key prove the user sees the intended translated message; a bare raises passes even when the key is missing from strings.json.

clusters.rule: Keep a pull request to its stated change: a requirements bump, an unrelated test refactor or a fixture rename does not belong in a PR whose title and description promise something else.
clusters.trigger: A diff carrying changes unrelated to the PR's title and description - a manifest requirement bump under a feature title, or fixture renames and parametrization restructuring alongside a small fix.
clusters.rationale: Reviewers ask for the diff to match the title so the change can be reviewed, and reverted, as one unit.

clusters.rule: Every unifiprotect code path reachable with an API-key-only client must work without the private bootstrap: resolve the needed identity at setup or omit the optional field, and give device-added dispatch a public-bootstrap equivalent covered by a test that starts from an empty bootstrap.
clusters.trigger: An entity constructor, DeviceInfo build or websocket add/adopt handler that dereferences api.bootstrap or private-bootstrap tracking (e.g. _pending_camera_ids) on a path also used by API-key-only clients.
clusters.rationale: The public API client has no bootstrap at all, so any dereference of it raises for those users while private-key installs look fine in review.

clusters.rule: A select entity's current_option must always be one of its advertised options; fall back to a valid option and log when the device reports an unknown value.
clusters.trigger: self._attr_current_option assigned from a dict .get() lookup keyed on a device-supplied value, with no handling of the None result.
clusters.rationale: A current_option outside the advertised options makes the select unusable in the frontend, so an unmapped device value needs a valid fallback and a log line.

clusters.rule: Collections surfaced to the frontend (select options, websocket payloads) must be ordered deterministically, e.g. sorted, rather than inheriting dict or matcher load order.
clusters.trigger: _attr_options or a websocket command response built by iterating a library dict, registry, or matcher list without an explicit sort.
clusters.rationale: Dict, registry and matcher iteration order is not stable across restarts, so unsorted collections reshuffle in the UI and make snapshots flap.

clusters.rule: Entity availability must follow both the coordinator's last_update_success and the continued presence of the backing object in the current bootstrap, not just incoming websocket messages.
clusters.trigger: An entity that subscribes to per-object websocket updates and sets _attr_available = data.last_update_success inside that callback, without a subscription to coordinator status or a presence check for the object.
clusters.rationale: An entity that tracks only its own websocket messages stays 'available' after the connection dies or after the object disappears from the bootstrap.

clusters.rule: A translated UpdateFailed must use a translation key written for the update path and pass the underlying error text as the placeholder, never a hardcoded generic string.
clusters.trigger: _async_update_data raising UpdateFailed with a translation_key borrowed from a service/action error and translation_placeholders set to a literal message.
clusters.rationale: Reusing an action's translation key with a literal placeholder produces a sentence written for a different context and hides the real error text from the user.

clusters.rule: entity_registry_enabled_default must be decided from the entity's identity, not from whether the device currently reports a value for it.
clusters.trigger: dataclasses.replace(description, entity_registry_enabled_default=...) combining a key check with description.value_fn(data) is not None.
clusters.rationale: entity_registry_enabled_default is read once at registration, so deciding it from the current reading makes an entity's existence depend on whatever the device happened to report at setup.

clusters.rule: async_turn_on must never write a device value that switches the device off; clamp a brightness of 0 to the minimum non-zero value or reject it.
clusters.trigger: A light async_turn_on that converts ATTR_BRIGHTNESS with brightness_to_value and guards the minimum with a truthiness check such as `if brightness:`.
clusters.rationale: async_turn_on writing a zero brightness switches the device off, so the service reports success while the light goes dark.

clusters.rule: Integration entity description subclasses must only add new fields; do not re-declare attributes the base EntityDescription already provides, such as SelectEntityDescription.options.
clusters.trigger: A frozen dataclass extending a platform EntityDescription that declares a field with the same name as one defined on the base class.
clusters.rationale: Re-declaring a base field in a frozen dataclass shadows the platform's own definition and its default, silently changing core behaviour for that description.

clusters.rule: Intent handlers must catch HomeAssistantError/ServiceValidationError specifically and re-raise IntentHandleError chained with `from err`, never a broad except with `from None`.
clusters.trigger: An intent handler wrapping a service call in `except Exception` and raising IntentHandleError with a formatted message and `from None`.
clusters.rationale: A broad except with `from None` swallows the underlying Home Assistant error and its translation, leaving the user with a generic intent failure.

clusters.rule: Directional transitional states must map to distinct icons in icons.json, matching how cover distinguishes opening from closing.
clusters.trigger: An icons.json state block that adds both `opening` and `closing` (or equivalent paired transitional states) pointing at the same mdi icon.
clusters.rationale: Cover already distinguishes opening from closing, and reusing one icon for both leaves users unable to tell direction at a glance.

clusters.rule: Do not feature-detect attributes on the integration's own pinned library with hasattr/getattr/callable; the manifest requirement pins the version, so call the API directly.
clusters.trigger: A setup or platform filter such as `if callable(getattr(node, "method", None))` applied to objects from the integration's requirement package.
clusters.rationale: manifest.json pins the requirement version, so hasattr/callable probes hide an outdated pin instead of failing loudly.

clusters.rule: Diagnostics output should expose internal library and connection data that is not otherwise reachable, not a dump of device and entity registry information.
clusters.trigger: async_get_config_entry_diagnostics building lists of device names with their entities from the device/entity registry.
clusters.rationale: Device and entity registry contents are already downloadable elsewhere; diagnostics exist to expose the library and connection state that is otherwise unreachable.

clusters.rule: Set only the _attr_* entity attributes; do not additionally assign the legacy private counterparts such as _name alongside _attr_name.
clusters.trigger: An entity __init__ assigning both self._attr_name and self._name (or another duplicated legacy attribute) to the same value.
clusters.rationale: The legacy private attributes are dead once _attr_* is set, and keeping both invites the two to diverge.

clusters.rule: Every translation_key an entity references must have a matching entry under `entity` in the integration's strings.json, added in the same PR and never removed while the key is still used.
clusters.trigger: A new or renamed entity description whose translation_key has no strings.json entry, or a strings.json diff deleting the `name` under a key that code still sets as translation_key.
clusters.rationale: A missing entry leaves the entity with an untranslated or empty name in every language, which surfaces to users as a nameless entity.

clusters.rule: Entities whose state is bool | None need tests that separate missing data (unknown) from an explicit zero/false reading.
clusters.trigger: A new is_on/native_value property returning None for absent data and a boolean otherwise, with fixtures covering only the populated case.
clusters.rationale: Without a fixture for the absent case the unknown branch is never executed, so the very confusion the property exists to prevent goes untested.

clusters.rule: Normalize loosely typed device API values explicitly: compare feature flags and on/off states against the full set of representations the API uses (True, 1, "1") instead of relying on truthiness or a partial literal set.
clusters.trigger: Entity gating written as `if not all(coordinator.get_value(path) ...)` or a state check written as `value in (True, "1")` against a JSON API that also returns ints and numeric strings.
clusters.rationale: This API returns True, 1 and "1" for the same flag, so truthiness or a partial literal set silently mis-reads some devices.

clusters.rule: Declare list-valued service schema fields with a real voluptuous list validator such as vol.All(cv.ensure_list, [str]), never with a bare Python type annotation like list[str].
clusters.trigger: A vol.Schema in an integration's services.py using a typing construct (list[str], dict[str, str]) as the validator for a Required/Optional key.
clusters.rationale: A typing construct is not callable as a voluptuous validator, so the schema silently accepts anything instead of validating the list.

clusters.rule: Resolve a config entry from a service call with the core helper homeassistant.helpers.service.async_get_config_entry instead of hand-rolling entry-exists / correct-domain / loaded-state checks in the integration.
clusters.trigger: An integration service handler defining its own _async_get_config_entry-style function that looks up hass.config_entries by id and raises ServiceValidationError for missing/unloaded entries.
clusters.rationale: homeassistant.helpers.service.async_get_config_entry already produces the correct translated ServiceValidationError for missing, wrong-domain and unloaded entries, and hand-rolled versions drift away from it.

clusters.rule: When an entity platform method maps a Home Assistant enum value onto a vendor constant, validate membership before indexing and raise HomeAssistantError, so an unsupported mode never escapes as a raw KeyError.
clusters.trigger: An async_set_* entity method indexing a module-level HA-to-vendor mapping dict (e.g. HVAC_TO_WF_MODE[hvac_mode]) inside a try block that only catches library or ValueError exceptions.
clusters.rationale: An unsupported mode indexing the vendor map escapes as a KeyError traceback instead of a message telling the user the mode is not supported.

clusters.rule: Do not add strings.json entries or icons for preset modes that already exist as core common presets; use the core PRESET_* constants in code and let the built-in translations and icons apply.
clusters.trigger: New state_attributes.preset_mode entries in an integration's strings.json or icons.json naming standard presets such as eco, comfort, away, boost.
clusters.rationale: Core already ships translations and icons for the common presets, so integration-level copies fragment the wording users see across integrations.

clusters.rule: Do not create entities for static device metadata; firmware version, mDNS name and similar constants belong in the device registry entry, not in the state machine.
clusters.trigger: A new sensor entity description whose value is a device identity or configuration constant (firmware version, mdns name, serial, IP) rather than a changing measurement, even under EntityCategory.DIAGNOSTIC.
clusters.rationale: Static values belong on the device registry entry; as entities they occupy the state machine and the recorder forever without ever changing.

clusters.rule: Key an entity's icons.json entry by the exact translation_key set on its entity description, not by the sensor's internal key.
clusters.trigger: An added icons.json entity key under a platform that does not literally match the translation_key of the corresponding EntityDescription.
clusters.rationale: Icon lookup is keyed by translation_key, so an entry keyed on the description's internal key never applies.

clusters.rule: Bound any integration-held cache keyed by a client- or peer-supplied identifier with a global cap or TTL, not just a per-key size limit.
clusters.trigger: A dict on an integration object indexed by an externally supplied id (session id, request id) that is written on inbound messages and only pruned per entry.
clusters.rationale: A dict keyed by a value the remote peer chooses grows without limit, and a per-entry cap does not stop a peer from creating unlimited entries.

clusters.rule: Include the idle notification value 0 in not_states for Z-Wave notification binary sensors so the entity clears when the device reports idle.
clusters.trigger: A NotificationZWaveJSEntityDescription whose not_states set lists only the specific event enum members and omits 0.
clusters.rationale: Z-Wave devices signal 'no longer detected' with notification value 0, so omitting it from not_states leaves the binary sensor stuck on.

clusters.rule: Adding a NewZWaveDiscoverySchema for a value that a legacy DISCOVERY_SCHEMAS entry already matches must preserve the existing entities: set allow_multi and adjust the legacy catch-all's not_states, or migrate the whole notification type and add it to MIGRATED_NOTIFICATION_TYPES.
clusters.trigger: A new NewZWaveDiscoverySchema entry in zwave_js covering a notification value or command class that legacy discovery schemas already produce entities for.
clusters.rationale: Legacy discovery schemas already create entities for these values, so a new schema without allow_multi or a migration entry silently deletes or duplicates entities users already have.

clusters.rule: Gate a report_usage deprecation warning on the deprecated condition actually being present, so callers that do not use the deprecated pattern never see it logged.
clusters.trigger: A report_usage call with breaks_in_ha_version placed on a common code path in core helpers without a check that the deprecated feature is in use.
clusters.rationale: A deprecation warning on a common code path fires for integrations that are not doing anything deprecated, which trains everyone to ignore it.

clusters.rule: Keep a guard that prevents a registry's _async_load from running more than once.
clusters.trigger: Removal of the loaded-event assertions or any other once-only guard from a registry _async_load in homeassistant/helpers.
clusters.rationale: Loading a registry a second time discards in-memory state written between the two loads, so the once-only guard is what makes the registry safe.

clusters.rule: Do not assume a sibling registry is set up when one registry helper calls another; guard dr.async_get / er.async_get so lookups still work with mocked or partially initialised registries.
clusters.trigger: A new dr.async_get(self._hass) or er.async_get(hass) call added inside an entity_registry or device_registry method that previously touched only its own data.
clusters.rationale: Registries are set up independently and tests frequently mock only one of them, so a helper that assumes the sibling exists breaks in contexts that used to work.

clusters.rule: Do not key a long-lived registry or cache by entity_id; entity_id changes at runtime on registry rename, so track the key used at insert time or keep it in sync on entity_id updates.
clusters.trigger: A module-level or hass-data dict indexed by entity.entity_id in async_added_to_hass and deleted by entity.entity_id in async_will_remove_from_hass.
clusters.rationale: entity_id changes when a user renames an entity, so anything keyed by it leaks the old key and loses track of the entity.

clusters.rule: Match entity registry entries on domain and platform in addition to unique_id; unique_id alone is not unique across integrations.
clusters.trigger: An entity_registry_updated event handler or registry lookup whose condition tests only entry.unique_id against a set of known ids.
clusters.rationale: unique_id is only unique within an integration's platform, so a lookup on unique_id alone matches entities belonging to unrelated integrations.

clusters.rule: Keep the dependency between core helper modules one-way: do not add a top-level import that closes a cycle between helpers modules; use a function-local import or move the logic into the module that already owns the dependency.
clusters.trigger: A new top-level `from .<helper> import ...` in homeassistant/helpers/ where the imported module already imports the importing one.
clusters.rationale: homeassistant/helpers is imported during bootstrap in a fixed order, so a cycle becomes an ImportError that appears only for some entry points.

clusters.rule: Use plain string values, not enum members, in selector option and mode lists so voluptuous validation errors show the user-facing string rather than an enum repr.
clusters.trigger: A selector constant in homeassistant/helpers/selector.py listing StrEnum members that are later fed to vol.In or exposed in a selector config.
clusters.rationale: Voluptuous renders the offending value in its error message, so an enum member shows the user a Python repr instead of the option they typed.

clusters.rule: When deprecating a Python dependency, update DEPRECATED_PACKAGES in homeassistant/requirements.py and the FORBIDDEN_PACKAGES entry in script/hassfest/requirements.py together, including the replacement package named in the reason text.
clusters.trigger: A change to the DEPRECATED_PACKAGES dict in homeassistant/requirements.py with no matching change to FORBIDDEN_PACKAGES in script/hassfest/requirements.py.
clusters.rationale: requirements.py warns at runtime and hassfest blocks at CI, so if only one of them knows about the deprecation the package keeps arriving in new integrations.

clusters.rule: Keep the pylint plugin README's description of a checker's accepted and rejected patterns exactly in step with the checker implementation and its test cases.
clusters.trigger: A change to pylint/plugins/README.md or a checker module docstring describing which code shapes the checker accepts, without a matching implementation or test in pylint/plugins/pylint_home_assistant/checkers/.
clusters.rationale: The README is what contributors read to understand what the checker rejects, so a description that no longer matches the implementation misleads everyone the checker fires on.

clusters.rule: Custom pylint checkers must key on the exact AST shape they target: handle the keyword form (service_func=) as well as the positional argument, and inspect the argument node type rather than merely counting arguments.
clusters.trigger: A checker helper extracting a handler from hass.services.async_register / async_register_admin_service by call.args index only, or a condition such as `if node.args and not has_translation_key` that never inspects the node type.
clusters.rationale: A checker matching on argument position or count alone both misses valid registrations and fires on code it was never meant to reject, and every false hit costs every contributor time.

clusters.rule: Keep file-glob constants in script/ tooling identical to the paths: filter of the GitHub workflow that invokes them.
clusters.trigger: A TRACKED_PATTERNS-style glob tuple in script/ that is narrower than the paths: filter of the corresponding .github/workflows/*.yml.
clusters.rationale: If the script's globs are narrower than the workflow's paths filter, CI runs the check on changes the script then ignores and the gap is invisible.

clusters.rule: New hassfest validation must ship with hassfest tests exercising both the valid case and each distinct failure mode it can report.
clusters.trigger: A new validation branch in script/hassfest/*.py that adds an error message, with no corresponding case added under tests/hassfest/.
clusters.rationale: hassfest errors gate every new integration, so each distinct message needs a case proving it fires only when it should.

clusters.rule: When a config flow gains a fallback path, add a test for its success case end to end, not only for the error case that motivated it.
clusters.trigger: A new branch in an integration's config_flow.py that calls the client on a cache miss, with test_config_flow.py changes covering only the failure outcome.
clusters.rationale: The fallback exists in order to succeed, so a test covering only the error that motivated it never proves the new path produces a working entry.

clusters.rule: When a platform converts raw API values into device_class or state_class enums, add a test feeding a missing or invalid value and assert setup does not raise and the entity is still created with the attribute unset.
clusters.trigger: New SensorDeviceClass/SensorStateClass enum lookups on payload data in an integration's sensor.py, with tests covering only well-formed payloads.
clusters.rationale: Device payloads carry units and classes the enums do not have, and the repo's expectation is that setup still completes with the attribute unset rather than raising.

clusters.rule: Do not assert exact library call counts during setup; assert the resulting device and entity registry state instead.
clusters.trigger: An assertion of the form `assert mock_client.<method>.call_count == N` in an integration test covering config entry setup.
clusters.rationale: Call counts change whenever setup is refactored, while the device and entity registry state is the behaviour the test actually cares about.

clusters.rule: A test's name and docstring must describe exactly the platform, service and outcome its assertions cover; when a copied or parametrized test disagrees with its body, fix whichever of the two is wrong before merge.
clusters.trigger: A module or test docstring naming a different platform, service, or exception than the file/body asserts - including a docstring copied from a neighbouring test, or one describing only a subset of the parametrize list.
clusters.rationale: Docstrings are how the next contributor decides which test covers what, so a stale one hides that a case is not covered at all.

clusters.rule: Drive a test's expected end state with a realistic mock sequence (raise once, then return data) rather than an always-raising mock that reaches the expected state only through internal retry or swallowing.
clusters.trigger: A test parametrized over ConfigEntryState.LOADED whose client mock has an unconditional side_effect exception on the data-fetch method.
clusters.rationale: An always-raising mock that still ends in the expected state proves the retry or the swallow happened, not that the integration reaches that state legitimately.

clusters.rule: Tests must use the integration's and core's own constants and helpers - DOMAIN, CONF_*, STATE_*, identifier helpers - wherever a value has a name, including as the key of the config dict passed to async_setup_component and in config entry data and options.
clusters.trigger: A raw string literal such as the domain name, "unavailable" or a config/option key in a test or conftest where the integration or homeassistant.const already defines a constant, or an identifier recomputed inline where the integration has a helper.
clusters.rationale: Literals in tests keep passing after the constant they mirror is renamed, so the test stops testing the integration's actual keys.

clusters.rule: Do not stack repeated await hass.async_block_till_done() calls to make a fixture settle; use a single deterministic wait or document why more than one pass is required.
clusters.trigger: Two or more consecutive `await hass.async_block_till_done()` statements in a test or conftest fixture.
clusters.rationale: Stacked block_till_done calls are a guess about how many event loop passes are needed and hide the real ordering problem.

clusters.rule: Mock an integration's library with AsyncMock-based fixtures rather than hand-written fake client classes.
clusters.trigger: A new conftest.py defining a stub class that reimplements the vendor library's properties and setters instead of patching the client with AsyncMock.
clusters.rationale: Hand-written fake clients drift from the library's real surface; the repo's pattern is patching the client with AsyncMock so a signature change fails the tests.

clusters.rule: When core code branches on whether the caller is a built-in integration (module starting with homeassistant.components.), test both the warning branch and the suppression branch.
clusters.trigger: A new report/warning in homeassistant/ that is skipped for modules under homeassistant.components., with tests asserting only the warning case.
clusters.rationale: The suppression for modules under homeassistant.components is the point of the change, so leaving it untested means nothing proves built-in integrations stay quiet.

clusters.rule: Match the mock to the real callable: patch coroutine functions with new_callable=AsyncMock (a plain patch(..., return_value=...) yields a non-awaitable MagicMock), patch synchronous ones with MagicMock, and never spec a whole library object as AsyncMock when it also exposes synchronous listener or registration methods.
clusters.trigger: patch("<library>.<Class>.<async_method>", return_value=...) without new_callable=AsyncMock, or a patch / AsyncMock(spec=...) / fixture annotation whose sync-vs-async kind does not match the awaited-ness of the target in the integration code.
clusters.rationale: A mismatched mock either fails to await or turns a synchronous registration into a coroutine nobody awaits, so the test exercises a code path that cannot occur in production.

clusters.rule: Do not write generated entity_ids into tests by hand: resolve the entity through the entity registry by unique_id or config entry and assert on the resolved id, including when asserting that an entity was not created.
clusters.trigger: A literal entity_id string built from a device name slug, or an assertion that `hass.states.get("<domain>.<guessed_slug>") is None`, especially for names whose characters change the slug ("2+", "2-way").
clusters.rationale: Slug generation depends on the device name and on core's slugify rules, so a hand-written id can pass for the wrong reason or silently stop matching.

clusters.rule: Assert that `hass.states.get(entity_id)` returned a state object before dereferencing `.state`.
clusters.trigger: A test chains `hass.states.get(...).state` in an assertion or comprehension without a preceding `is not None` check.
clusters.rationale: hass.states.get returns None for an entity that was never created, and the resulting AttributeError hides which entity is actually missing.

clusters.rule: Every parameter of a test function, including injected fixtures, must carry a type annotation.
clusters.trigger: A new `async def test_*` adds a fixture parameter (e.g. `mock_growatt_v1_api`) with no annotation while its siblings are annotated.
clusters.rationale: The repo requires fully annotated tests so fixture types are checked, and one unannotated parameter opts the whole function out.

clusters.rule: When new entities are added, regenerate and commit the snapshot files, and keep any hard-coded expected entity list in the same order the entity descriptions are iterated during setup.
clusters.trigger: A PR adds entity descriptions to a platform's description tuple and adds matching entries to a test's expected-entity list or snapshot assertion.
clusters.rationale: Snapshots must be regenerated rather than reasoned about, and a hand-maintained expected list only stays correct if it follows the order the descriptions are iterated during setup.

clusters.rule: Do not land test scaffolding nothing consumes: conftest fixtures, JSON fixture files, module-level TEST_* constants and fixture parameters in a test signature must each be referenced by a test in the same PR, or removed.
clusters.trigger: A diff adding a fixture, a file under tests/components/*/fixtures/, a helper such as init_*_integration, or a test-signature parameter (snapshot, a client/coordinator fixture) that no test in the diff references - or leaving one behind after the test that used it changed.
clusters.rationale: Unused fixtures read as coverage that does not exist and rot until nobody knows whether they still describe the integration.

clusters.rule: Shared mock/data construction repeated across tests belongs in a pytest fixture in conftest.py, not in module-level builder functions each test calls manually.
clusters.trigger: A test module defines a helper like `build_homeegrams()` or inline mock-client wiring and calls it in an identical setup block before `setup_integration` in several tests.
clusters.rationale: Identical mock wiring repeated before setup_integration in several tests is what conftest fixtures are for, and duplicated wiring drifts per test.

clusters.rule: Timestamps passed to `freezer.move_to()` must carry an explicit timezone offset when the assertions depend on local-time conversion.
clusters.trigger: A test calls `freezer.move_to("YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM:SS")` with no `Z`/`+00:00` suffix while the code under test branches on `dt_util.now().hour`.
clusters.rationale: A naive timestamp is interpreted in the machine's local zone, so the test passes or fails depending on where CI runs.

clusters.rule: Stateless entity triggers must accept STATE_UNKNOWN as a valid from_state so the first real event after startup fires, matching button entity trigger semantics.
clusters.trigger: A trigger implementation or its parametrized tests treat an `unknown` -> first-matching-state transition as not triggering for a stateless domain (event, button).
clusters.rationale: Event and button entities are unknown until their first event, so refusing unknown as a from_state means the trigger never fires after a restart.

clusters.rule: Service actions that resolve a device_id must have test coverage for the device being absent from the device registry, and should raise ServiceValidationError rather than failing silently.
clusters.trigger: A new service handler takes `device_id` and looks it up in the device registry, with tests only covering the happy path and backend errors.
clusters.rationale: Users pass device ids from automations that outlive the device, and the repo expects a ServiceValidationError rather than a silent no-op.

clusters.rule: Assert that a specific mocked method was or was not awaited instead of inspecting `mock.mock_calls[-1]`.
clusters.trigger: A test indexes into `mock_calls` (e.g. `mock_calls[-1][0] != "send_start_impulse_async"`) to prove a call did not happen.
clusters.rationale: Indexing mock_calls asserts on call ordering internals, while assert_not_awaited names the method and survives unrelated calls.

clusters.rule: Parametrized tests for capability/feature flag enums must cover the combined-flags and zero/empty value, not only the single-flag cases.
clusters.trigger: A platform change alters how bitwise capability flags are interpreted while the test parametrization lists only individual enum members.
clusters.rationale: Bitwise capability flags arrive combined in practice and the zero value is what an unknown device reports, so single-member parametrization misses the cases that actually occur.

clusters.rule: After firing a coordinator's update timer with `async_fire_time_changed`, await `hass.async_block_till_done(wait_background_tasks=True)` before asserting on refreshed state.
clusters.trigger: A test ticks the freezer by the coordinator UPDATE_INTERVAL, calls `async_fire_time_changed`, then asserts entity state after a plain `await hass.async_block_till_done()`.
clusters.rationale: Coordinator refreshes run as background tasks, so a plain block_till_done returns before the new data reaches the entity and the assertion races.

clusters.rule: Run the translation generation script for the integration and re-capture entity snapshots after adding translation keys, so snapshotted entities show their translated names and object-id-derived entity_ids.
clusters.trigger: A snapshot .ambr adds entities with a `translation_key` set but `original_name: None`, no `object_id_base`, and generic entity_ids like `sensor.device_1_2`.
clusters.rationale: Entity names and object-id-derived entity_ids only appear once translations are generated, so a snapshot taken before that records placeholder ids users will never see.

clusters.rule: Do not snapshot volatile numeric sensor readings; snapshot the stable entity metadata (entity id, device class, unit, availability) and relax the fluctuating `state` value.
clusters.trigger: A dependency bump changes numeric `state` values inside a snapshot .ambr file, forcing snapshot churn.
clusters.rationale: Snapshotting a fluctuating reading turns every dependency bump into snapshot churn that reviewers cannot meaningfully check.

clusters.rule: Snapshot the device registry entry once per test module, not once per entity.
clusters.trigger: A per-platform test loops over entity registry entries and snapshots the resolved `device_entry` inside the loop.
clusters.rationale: The device entry is the same for every entity of the device, so snapshotting it inside the entity loop multiplies the .ambr for no extra coverage.

clusters.rule: A regenerated snapshot must contain exactly one entity per unique_id for a config entry; prune stale blocks instead of committing duplicates.
clusters.trigger: A snapshot .ambr contains two entries sharing a unique_id under different entity_ids.
clusters.rationale: Two entity_ids sharing a unique_id in a snapshot means the regenerated file kept a stale block, which then masks a real duplicate-registration bug.

clusters.rule: A test must actually exercise the failure path named in its name and docstring; patch the dependency with a failing `side_effect` rather than a benign empty result that duplicates an existing test.
clusters.trigger: A config flow test named for a startup/discovery failure patches the discovery helper to return an empty result and asserts a generic abort reason.
clusters.rationale: A test named for a failure that patches a benign empty result duplicates an existing test and leaves the failure path uncovered.

clusters.rule: Tests that enable a disabled-by-default entity must advance time to run the coordinator refresh and assert the entity's resolved value, not merely that the entity exists.
clusters.trigger: A test enables an entity via the entity registry and reloads, then only asserts `state is not None`.
clusters.rationale: Enabling the entity only proves it exists; without advancing time for the refresh, the value the entity was disabled for is never asserted.

clusters.rule: Obtain registries through the provided pytest fixtures (`entity_registry: er.EntityRegistry`, `device_registry`, `issue_registry`) declared as test/fixture parameters, not by calling `er.async_get(hass)` inside the body.
clusters.trigger: A test or conftest fixture body calls `er.async_get(hass)` / `dr.async_get(hass)` instead of taking the registry fixture.
clusters.rationale: The registry fixtures are the repo's standard way to obtain registries and keep that setup visible in the signature.

clusters.rule: Assert that a specific repair issue key is absent rather than that the whole issue registry is empty.
clusters.trigger: A test asserts `len(issue_registry.issues) == 0` or compares the full issue registry contents.
clusters.rationale: Asserting the whole registry is empty breaks whenever an unrelated issue is added and still does not prove the issue under test is gone.

clusters.rule: Deprecation repair issues must have test coverage for every branch that selects a different translation key, including the entity-used-in-automations/scripts variant and its placeholder substitution.
clusters.trigger: A repairs test only covers the plain deprecated-entity issue while the implementation also raises a `*_scripts`/`*_automations` variant with an `{items}` placeholder.
clusters.rationale: The automations/scripts variants carry their own translation key and placeholder substitution, which is exactly where these repair issues break.

clusters.rule: When a change tightens validation, fix the existing tests it breaks instead of deleting them.
clusters.trigger: A diff that adds stricter validation also removes an existing test function.
clusters.rationale: Deleting the test that the stricter validation broke removes the only record of what the old behaviour was and of who relied on it.

clusters.rule: When a service response model gains fields, add a test case where those fields carry non-default values rather than only the default None case.
clusters.trigger: A test's expected service-response dict gains new keys whose asserted values are all `None`.
clusters.rationale: A response test whose new fields are all None passes even when those fields are never populated.

clusters.rule: A test parametrized over a fixture name must take that fixture as a function parameter; otherwise drop the parametrization.
clusters.trigger: @pytest.mark.parametrize("<fixture_name>", [...]) - mqtt_config_entry_data, clients_all_payload - above a test whose signature omits that name.
clusters.rationale: Without the parameter the override never reaches the fixture, so the test silently runs the default case once per param and appears to cover more than it does.

clusters.rule: Unique_id migration tests must round-trip every unique_id format the integration produces (device, multi-channel and group variants) and must not let one format's pattern match another's ids.
clusters.trigger: A migration test derives old-format unique_ids with string slicing/suffix matching and skips entries where the channel is None.
clusters.rationale: Each unique_id format has to survive the migration, and slicing-based helpers let one format's pattern match another's ids, masking a broken migration.

clusters.rule: Tests for a trigger or condition must cover the full domain matrix its implementation accepts: every supported entity domain, plus a negative case proving unsupported domains do not match.
clusters.trigger: A new trigger/condition test parametrized over a single domain (e.g. only "person") while the implementation also handles device_tracker or others, or covering only supported domains with no unsupported-entity case, including under behavior='all'.
clusters.rationale: Domain filtering is where these helpers go wrong, and a single-domain test proves nothing about the filter.

clusters.rule: Matter node fixtures must list any cluster whose attributes they define in that endpoint's Descriptor ServerList.
clusters.trigger: A `tests/components/matter/fixtures/nodes/*.json` adds attributes for a cluster id that is absent from the endpoint's `65531` server list.
clusters.rationale: Home Assistant discovers Matter entities from the endpoint's Descriptor ServerList, so a fixture with attributes for an unlisted cluster describes a device that cannot exist.

clusters.rule: Setup-failure tests must assert the exception whose retry semantics match the intent: ConfigEntryNotReady when setup should be retried, ConfigEntryError when the failure is fatal.
clusters.trigger: A test named or documented as "not ready" asserts ConfigEntryError (or vice versa) around async_setup_entry.
clusters.rationale: ConfigEntryNotReady and ConfigEntryError mean retry and give up; asserting the wrong one lets setup behaviour that strands users pass review.

clusters.rule: Service-call tests must pass values that are valid under the service schema (the integration's direction/mode constants), not stand-in primitives.
clusters.trigger: A test invokes an integration service or helper with integers/placeholders where the service schema expects domain constants such as DIR_LEFT/DIR_UP.
clusters.rationale: A test passing an integer where the schema requires a direction constant exercises a call the service itself would have rejected.

clusters.rule: Bluetooth integration tests must drive the integration through the public injection helpers (e.g. inject_bluetooth_service_info) rather than calling a coordinator's private _async_handle_bluetooth_event.
clusters.trigger: A test calls coordinator._async_handle_bluetooth_event(...) or another underscore-prefixed coordinator callback to simulate an advertisement.
clusters.rationale: inject_bluetooth_service_info drives the same path a real advertisement takes, while calling the coordinator's private callback skips the bluetooth manager entirely.

clusters.rule: Do not re-serialize existing JSON test fixtures; leave non-ASCII text as literal UTF-8 rather than \u escapes.
clusters.trigger: A diff in tests/components/*/fixtures/*.json rewrites accented characters as \uXXXX escapes or otherwise reformats untouched fixture lines.
clusters.rationale: Reformatting an untouched fixture buries the actual change in a diff nobody can review.

clusters.rule: Tests must not assert known-incorrect integration behavior as the expected value; leave the assertion out or mark it xfail until the integration is fixed.
clusters.trigger: A parametrized test case is accompanied by a comment calling the expected value a known bug or a follow-up fix.
clusters.rationale: An assertion that encodes a known bug becomes the specification and stops the fix from being noticed.

clusters.rule: Patch third-party helpers at the integration's import site (homeassistant.components.<domain>.<name>) rather than patching the library or stdlib module globally.
clusters.trigger: A test calls patch("shutil.which", ...) or patch("<library>.<func>", ...) for a symbol the integration imported into its own module namespace.
clusters.rationale: The integration imported the symbol into its own module namespace, so patching the origin module does not affect it while patching globally affects unrelated code.

clusters.rule: Give each entity a translation_key so its name (and therefore its entity_id suffix) is distinct from the device name instead of the entity_id collapsing to button.<device>.
clusters.trigger: A new entity snapshot shows original_name/object_id_base as None and an entity_id equal to the bare device or container slug.
clusters.rationale: An entity with no name collapses its entity_id to the bare device slug, which collides as soon as the device gains a second entity on that platform.

clusters.rule: Media source tests must construct MediaSourceItem with the integration's own DOMAIN and a bare item identifier, not another integration's domain or a full media-source:// URI.
clusters.trigger: MediaSourceItem(hass, "<other-domain>", f"{media_source.URI_SCHEME}{DOMAIN}", ...) in a media source test.
clusters.rationale: The domain and identifier are what the media source resolves against, so a foreign domain or a full media-source:// URI tests a call the framework never makes.

clusters.rule: Recorder platform unit-conversion maps must be string-to-string; do not use None keys or empty-string units in the mapping.
clusters.trigger: A recorder platform test or implementation supplies a unit map entry like {None: ""} where the annotation is dict[str, dict[str, str]].
clusters.rationale: The mapping is annotated dict[str, dict[str, str]], so None keys and empty-string units break the conversion lookup at runtime.

clusters.rule: Syrupy .ambr files must be produced by running pytest --snapshot-update; never hand-write, hand-append or hand-edit snapshot blocks or their parametrization ids.
clusters.trigger: A diff to tests/components/*/snapshots/*.ambr that deviates from generator output - a manually written EntityRegistryEntrySnapshot block, a duplicated '# ---' divider, or a bracketed id ([megane_e-tech]) that does not match the parametrize source values.
clusters.rationale: A hand-edited snapshot asserts what the author believed rather than what the code produced, which is the one thing snapshots exist to prevent.

clusters.rule: Tests must not mutate a shared module-level CONFIG dict; copy it and set options on the nested integration config the integration actually reads.
clusters.trigger: A test assigns into a module-level CONFIG constant (config[CONF_X] = ...) rather than building a local copy of the nested domain config.
clusters.rationale: Mutating the shared constant leaks into every later test in the module and makes failures depend on test order.

clusters.rule: Import SnapshotAssertion from syrupy.assertion and snapshot_platform from tests.common; do not pull SnapshotAssertion out of tests.common.
clusters.trigger: A test file adds `from tests.common import SnapshotAssertion` (alone or alongside snapshot_platform).
clusters.rationale: SnapshotAssertion belongs to syrupy, and the re-export through tests.common is what the repo is trying to remove.

clusters.rule: Config entry migration tests must seed the entity registry with the entities a pre-migration install would already have, and assert they are re-associated with the new device or subentry.
clusters.trigger: A migration test asserts only that subentries/devices were created, without registering the old entities beforehand.
clusters.rationale: The migration exists to move entities users already have, so a test with no pre-existing entities never exercises the re-association at all.

clusters.rule: Tests must not branch on entity_id with if/elif to pick expected values; parametrize the expected state alongside the entity or use the snapshot_platform helper.
clusters.trigger: An if/elif chain inside a test loop selecting which assertion to run per entity_id.
clusters.rationale: Branching on entity_id inside a loop hides which entities were actually asserted and skips silently when an id changes.

clusters.rule: Helpers that mutate a BluetoothServiceInfoBleak must copy the existing manufacturer_data mapping and update only the target manufacturer id, not replace the whole dict.
clusters.trigger: A bluetooth test helper builds `{<mfr_id>: bytes(...)}` and assigns it as the full manufacturer_data.
clusters.rationale: Replacing the whole mapping drops the other manufacturers' data the parser depends on, so the helper builds an advertisement no real device would send.

clusters.rule: Each device entry added to a shared API fixture must use a unique deviceId rather than reusing an existing device's identifier.
clusters.trigger: A new object appended to tests/components/*/fixtures/*.json repeats a deviceId already present in the file.
clusters.rationale: Shared fixtures are keyed by deviceId, so a duplicate silently replaces the existing device instead of adding one.

clusters.rule: A mock or fixture must configure every library call and accessor the exercised path touches - including calls whose exceptions the integration suppresses, and the availability accessor the base entity reads - matching the fixture combination the integration's existing tests already use.
clusters.trigger: A test mocking one of a pair of related API calls (mock_setup_webhook without get_webhook_configuration), or a Mock(spec=<device class>) fixture omitting a *.return_value that the sibling fixtures in the same conftest set (e.g. get_online.return_value).
clusters.rationale: An unmocked call returns a MagicMock that happens to be truthy, so the test passes while the entity's real behaviour is never exercised.

clusters.rule: Replacement functions substituted for a library API in tests must accept *args and **kwargs so they match the real call surface.
clusters.trigger: A test defines a zero-argument stub (e.g. an async generator) that replaces a library method the integration calls with arguments.
clusters.rationale: A zero-argument stub raises TypeError as soon as the integration passes the arguments the real method takes, or quietly proves the call was made with none.

clusters.rule: Name a platform test after the Home Assistant service it calls rather than the underlying vendor concept.
clusters.trigger: A test that calls a service such as vacuum.clean_area is renamed to describe the implementation detail (test_clean_segments).
clusters.rationale: Tests are grouped by the Home Assistant service they cover, so naming one after the vendor concept hides which service is tested.

clusters.rule: Advance coordinator intervals with freezer.tick(...) followed by async_fire_time_changed(hass); do not pass a separately computed dt_util.utcnow() + timedelta timestamp.
clusters.trigger: async_fire_time_changed(hass, dt_util.utcnow() + timedelta(...)) in a test that also uses the freezer fixture.
clusters.rationale: A separately computed utcnow() drifts from the frozen clock, so the timer either fires twice or not at all.

clusters.rule: An empty-string unit from a device payload must be normalized to None (or mapped to a real unit) rather than surfacing as unit_of_measurement: ''.
clusters.trigger: A discovery path or fixture carries "unit": "" for a numeric datapoint and passes it through to the entity description.
clusters.rationale: An empty string is not a unit: it breaks unit conversion and displays a stray separator in the frontend.

clusters.rule: Tests that assert on debug log output must raise the level first with caplog.set_level(logging.DEBUG, logger="homeassistant.components.<domain>").
clusters.trigger: A test asserts a debug-level message appears in caplog.text without calling caplog.set_level for the integration's logger.
clusters.rationale: Debug records are not captured at the default level, so the assertion only passes when something else happened to raise it.

clusters.rule: Read entity metadata that is not exposed in the state through the entity registry, not by reaching into hass.data["entity_components"].
clusters.trigger: A test does hass.data["entity_components"]["<platform>"].get_entity(entity_id) to inspect an entity object.
clusters.rationale: hass.data["entity_components"] is internal bookkeeping; the entity registry is the supported way to read entity metadata.

clusters.rule: When an entity key change alters generated entity_ids, update every remaining reference to the old entity_id in the test module.
clusters.trigger: A parametrization renames sensor keys (device_cpu -> cpu) while other tests in the file still assert on the old entity_id string.
clusters.rationale: Renaming a key changes every generated entity_id in the module, and the remaining references then assert on entities that no longer exist.

clusters.rule: Never wait on wall-clock time with asyncio.sleep in tests; patch the delay or call_later so timers fire deterministically.
clusters.trigger: await asyncio.sleep(<n>) used to let a scheduled callback or timer fire in a test.
clusters.rationale: Wall-clock sleeps make the suite slow and flaky; timers have to be driven deterministically.

clusters.rule: Assert against concrete expected values (such as the generated proxy URL prefix) rather than comparing two attributes of the object under test, which holds by construction.
clusters.trigger: assert obj.attr_a == obj.attr_b where both come from the same entity under test and the implementation makes them equal.
clusters.rationale: The comment points out one assertion that is true by construction; 'do not write tautological assertions' is general testing advice rather than a Home Assistant convention.

clusters.rule: A snapshot_platform test for a platform that contains entities with entity_registry_enabled_default=False must apply @pytest.mark.usefixtures("entity_registry_enabled_by_default"), because snapshot_platform asserts disabled_by is None for every entity.
clusters.trigger: A new or edited test calls snapshot_platform(hass, entity_registry, snapshot, entry.entry_id) for a platform whose entity descriptions include entity_registry_enabled_default=False, without the entity_registry_enabled_by_default fixture.
clusters.rationale: snapshot_platform asserts disabled_by is None for every entity, so a platform with disabled-by-default entities either fails or snapshots a subset without the fixture.

clusters.rule: An entity registry snapshot whose 'aliases' field renders as list([None]) must be investigated as an entity-registration bug; aliases must be an empty set or a set of non-null strings.
clusters.trigger: A new .ambr snapshot contains "'aliases': list([\n None,\n ])" inside an EntityRegistryEntrySnapshot.
clusters.rationale: aliases is a set of user-defined names, so a None inside it means something passed a null through entity registration and will break alias lookup.

clusters.rule: A test that patches an API call to raise an authentication exception must assert that the reauth flow actually started (e.g. config_entry_reauth.assert_called_once()), not merely reference the mock.
clusters.trigger: A test injects an authentication exception via side_effect and references a reauth mock without calling an assertion method on it.
clusters.rationale: Referencing the mock without asserting on it proves nothing, and the point of the test is that the auth failure starts the reauth flow.

clusters.rule: Reconfigure-flow tests that submit only a subset of the config entry fields must assert that the omitted optional fields (credentials, tokens) are preserved on the entry.
clusters.trigger: A test_config_flow.py reconfigure test calls async_configure with a dict omitting CONF_USERNAME/CONF_PASSWORD or other optional entry keys and only asserts the flow result type.
clusters.rationale: Reconfigure rebuilds the entry data, so silently dropping stored credentials is exactly the regression these tests exist to catch.

clusters.rule: When firing async_fire_time_changed to trigger a coordinator refresh, capture the base time after the config entries are set up (or add a margin / use fire_all=True); a time captured before setup can land before the timer the entity scheduled.
clusters.trigger: A test assigns now = dt_util.now()/utcnow() before async_setup_component or hass.config_entries.async_setup, then calls async_fire_time_changed(hass, now + <scan interval>) and asserts on refresh call counts.
clusters.rationale: A timestamp captured before setup can be earlier than the timer the entity scheduled, so the fired event does not trigger the refresh and the assertion is a coin flip.

clusters.rule: Config entry migration tests must be named (and their docstring worded) for the exact version transition exercised, e.g. test_migrate_minor_version_1_to_2 rather than test_migrate_to_1_1.
clusters.trigger: A test in tests/components/*/test_init.py exercises async_migrate_entry / minor_version or version bumps but its name does not state the source and target version.
clusters.rationale: Migration tests accumulate one per version step, so the name has to say which transition it covers.

clusters.rule: Fixtures that build a MockConfigEntry must derive its title, data and options from the parametrizable config fixture rather than hard-coding literals.
clusters.trigger: A conftest.py fixture constructs MockConfigEntry(domain=DOMAIN, title="<literal>", ...) while a sibling get_config/mock_config fixture supplies the same value and can be overridden by tests.
clusters.rationale: Hard-coded title and data defeat the parametrizable config fixture, so tests that override it silently get the literal instead.

clusters.rule: Tests must address entities by their hard-coded entity ID (as captured in the snapshot) instead of looking the ID up dynamically from the entity registry.
clusters.trigger: A test calls er.async_entries_for_config_entry(...) and filters by domain/platform just to recover a single entity_id for a service call or state assertion.
clusters.rationale: Recovering a single entity_id by filtering the registry restates the implementation, while the snapshot already pins the id the test should address.

clusters.rule: Test docstrings must state only the behavior under test; do not narrate device model history, the prior bug, or the PR description in them.
clusters.trigger: A new test's docstring spans multiple paragraphs describing a specific device firmware quirk, the exception it used to raise, or the regression history.
clusters.rationale: Regression history belongs in the PR description; a docstring that narrates it stops describing what the test asserts.

clusters.rule: Changes to shared trigger/helper base classes must add coverage for subclasses that intentionally target STATE_UNKNOWN/STATE_UNAVAILABLE before excluding those states globally.
clusters.trigger: A diff makes an EntityTriggerBase-style helper skip unavailable/unknown states in match logic, and the accompanying tests only use an implementation whose is_valid_state() rejects those states.
clusters.rationale: Excluding unknown and unavailable in a shared base changes behaviour for every subclass, including those whose is_valid_state deliberately accepts those states.

clusters.rule: A fix for an async race must ship a regression test that actually drives both concurrent call paths; asserting a new private flag (e.g. script_obj._unloaded) does not substitute for reproducing the race.
clusters.trigger: A PR adds unload/teardown guard state to a helper and its test only asserts the private attribute instead of starting a run while the unload is in progress.
clusters.rationale: Asserting the new private flag only proves the flag exists; the race is only shown fixed by starting a run while the unload is in progress.

clusters.rule: Test cases added to the custom pylint quality-scale checkers must encode a rule the checker deliberately enforces; incidental matches produced by the implementation should be dropped or the implementation adjusted.
clusters.trigger: A new parametrized case in tests/pylint/quality_scale/ asserts a diagnostic on code whose flagged condition cannot occur in practice (e.g. _attr_unique_id assignment after a raise in __init__).
clusters.rationale: A test case that pins an incidental match makes the accident part of the checker's contract.

clusters.rule: Changes to the split_tests fixture-hashing logic must add coverage proving the hash changes when a shared helper module above or beside the chosen root is edited, not only for conftest.py files.
clusters.trigger: A diff modifies fixture-hash computation in script/split_tests and its tests only cover conftest.py edits and same-directory scope.
clusters.rationale: Invalidating the split when a shared helper changes is the whole point of the hash, and conftest-only tests never exercise that.

clusters.rule: End-to-end frontend tests must assert on the element of the specific step under test, not on the outer shell component that renders before its API call resolves.
clusters.trigger: A Playwright spec asserts only expect(page.locator("ha-onboarding")).toBeVisible() (or another shell element) after navigating, without waiting for the concrete step element.
clusters.rationale: The shell renders before the step's API call resolves, so asserting on it passes even when the step never appears.
